stories.headline: Amid uproar, FCRA Bill referred to JPC - The Tribune
stories.summary: An amended FCRA Bill has been referred to a joint parliamentary committee (JPC) after widespread opposition from Christian organisations and chief ministers of Mizoram, Meghalaya and Nagaland. Key concerns centre on provisions allowing government takeover of NGO assets when licences expire or are cancelled, and restrictions on foreign funding for religious conversions.

stories.headline: Kerala HC sets aside Centre's order refusing FCRA renewal to two NGOs over alleged Vizhinjam port protest funding - The Hindu
stories.summary: The Kerala High Court quashed the Centre's order denying FCRA renewal to two NGOs (Save A Family Plan and Kerala Social Service Forum) over alleged Vizhinjam port protest funding, ruling that the connection was too far-fetched and that peaceful protest is not an undesirable purpose under FCRA regulations. The court directed authorities to review and pass fresh orders within three months.

stories.headline: Mizoram churches rally against FCRA Bill, warn of threat to properties, NGOs
stories.summary: Churches in Mizoram held a mass rally opposing the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, warning that its provisions could lead to seizure of church properties and assets and threaten minority communities' rights.

stories.headline: News | Catholic Connect
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has criticized the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, warning that its provisions could expand executive control over NGOs and pose serious threats to Christian institutions providing healthcare, education and social welfare services. He argues the Bill raises constitutional concerns and calls for parliamentary scrutiny and civil society consultation before passage.

stories.headline: Centre addresses ‘myths’ and concerns over FCRA Bill
stories.summary: India's Ambassador to the US addresses concerns and "myths" about the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, clarifying that the law will not shut down legitimate civil society organisations but will strengthen oversight of foreign funding through better transparency and governance. He cites data showing foreign contributions to registered organisations have grown significantly and emphasizes that the law applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion or ideology.

stories.headline: US Congressman Warns India's FCRA Bill is a "Clear Attack on Christians"
stories.summary: A US Republican congressman has publicly criticized India's proposed Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill 2026, characterizing it as targeting Christians and restricting their rights.

stories.headline: Assam Christian Forum opposes proposed FCRA Amendment Bill
stories.summary: The Assam Christian Forum has expressed opposition to the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, which would impose stricter restrictions on foreign funding to NGOs and religious organizations in India.

stories.headline: News | Catholic Connect
stories.summary: The Indian government has issued clarifications regarding the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, stating that places of worship will retain their religious character and that designated authorities will only manage assets created from foreign contributions after FCRA registration lapses. The clarification addresses concerns raised by Christian organisations and the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India about potential adverse impacts on NGOs receiving foreign funding.

stories.headline: India: New foreign funding rules tighten control over civil society and undermine the right to freedom of association | ICJ
stories.summary: The International Commission of Jurists criticizes India's June 2026 amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Rules, arguing they grant the government excessive powers to control NGO activities and severely restrict foreign funding for human rights advocacy, policy research, and other critical civil society work, violating international human rights protections.

stories.headline: FCRA and NGOs: Rewriting the rulebook
stories.summary: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 represents a major overhaul of India's FCRA framework since 2010, introducing new government powers over foreign-funded assets and reshaping rules for overseas contributions to NGOs.

stories.headline: India plans to tighten rules on foreign-funded NGOs
stories.summary: India is proposing stricter regulations on foreign-funded NGOs and charities through new legislation, raising concerns among organizations that the rules could enable government asset seizures.

stories.headline: Building an Atmanirbhar philanthropy ecosystem - The Hindu
stories.summary: An opinion piece in The Hindu discussing the need to build a self-reliant Indian philanthropy ecosystem, likely addressing how India's funding and giving models can become more independent and sustainable domestically.

stories.headline: FCRA bill aims to bolster oversight, not target any religion: Centre | India News
stories.summary: The government defends the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, asserting it aims to strengthen oversight of foreign funding rather than target any religious community, amid concerns raised by Meghalaya's chief minister and Christian organizations including the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India.

stories.headline: SBI seeks rules for managing NGO funds if FCRA registration cancelled - The Tribune
stories.summary: SBI is requesting the government to establish clearer rules for managing NGO funds in cases where FCRA registration is cancelled, addressing a regulatory gap affecting financial institutions and NGOs.

stories.headline: FCRA Bill 2026: Why asset control, registration rules and government powers are raising concerns?
stories.summary: An explainer article examining key concerns raised by NGOs and other stakeholders about the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, focusing on asset control powers, registration renewal procedures, and broad administrative discretion that critics argue could burden smaller organisations.

stories.headline: The REAL Reason Opposition & NGO's are Panicking!
stories.summary: A social media post discussing the consequences for NGOs when FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered, or not renewed, specifically regarding properties and assets funded by foreign money.

stories.headline: Can the government take control of foreign-funded assets? The FCRA Bill explained
stories.summary: An explanatory news article examining how the FCRA (Foreign Contribution Regulation Act) Bill may allow the government to take control of assets funded by foreign contributions to NGOs and civil society organizations.

stories.headline: What Is The FCRA Bill 2026 And Why Is It Changing India's Foreign Funding Rules?
stories.summary: The article explains the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, which aims to establish clearer rules for managing assets created through foreign contributions when organisations lose their FCRA registration. The Bill has generated debate between the government, which emphasises transparency and oversight, and NGOs and religious organisations concerned about reduced autonomy and increased government control.

stories.headline: India’s Proposed FCRA Amendment Raises New Threats for Christian Ministries - International Christian Concern
stories.summary: India's proposed 2026 FCRA amendment would grant the government authority to seize and manage assets of NGOs, including Christian organizations, that lose or fail to renew their foreign funding registration. The bill raises concerns among religious freedom advocates about increased restrictions on Christian ministries and charitable organizations operating in India.

stories.headline: India's FCRA Amendment Rules 2026: A New Era for NGO Governance, ETLegalWorld
stories.summary: An expert analysis of India's FCRA Amendment Rules 2026, covering key changes including foreign national restrictions for key functionaries, purpose-specific and geography-specific registration requirements, instalment-based foreign contribution releases, and ultimate donor disclosure mandates.

stories.headline: FCRA Bill 2026 | Rigid rules - Editorial on tightened FCRA norms and their impact on NGOs - Telegraph India
stories.summary: An editorial criticises the Foreign Contribution Regulation (Amendment) Rules 2026 as the tenth amendment since 2011, arguing that while curbing fraudulent NGO activities is necessary, the new prescriptive requirements—including specific activity declarations, geographical restrictions, fee structures, and social media disclosure mandates—excessively constrain civil society autonomy and undermine democratic participation by creating fear of government sanctions for minor deviations.

stories.headline: Proselytisation Undefined, No Flexibility for Community Needs: New FCRA Rules Get Many Things Wrong - The Wire
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the new FCRA Amendment Rules impose excessive regulatory burdens on NGOs and religious institutions without clear legal definitions or flexibility, particularly affecting Christian organizations' ability to respond to community needs and creating uncertainty around undefined terms like 'proselytisation'.

stories.headline: US lawmaker raises concerns over FCRA Bill, warns of strain in bilateral ties
stories.summary: A US Congressman has raised concerns about India's proposed FCRA amendments, claiming they would enable government takeovers of churches and religious charities. The proposed changes have triggered mounting opposition in Mizoram, where churches, NGOs, and political parties are planning a demonstration on August 11.

stories.headline: Northeast Christian-dominant states add pressure on Centre over FCRA Bill
stories.summary: Christian-dominant states in the Northeast have heightened pressure on the central government over the FCRA Bill, with the Assam Christian Forum expressing concerns that the legislation could threaten religious freedom by allowing government oversight and management of religious institutions.

stories.headline: Nagaland Assembly Voices Concern Over Proposed FCRA Amendments
stories.summary: The Nagaland Legislative Assembly discussed concerns over proposed FCRA amendments, with multiple advisors and MLAs warning that the changes could harm churches, charitable organisations and minority-led social welfare institutions that have historically provided education, healthcare and community services across the state. The Chief Minister acknowledged these concerns and called for continued consultation with Christian leaders and stakeholders before finalising the legislation.

stories.headline: Mizoram Congress to Oppose the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, Until It is Withdrawn
stories.summary: The Mizoram Pradesh Congress Committee announced opposition to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, stating it would continue to oppose the proposed legislation until it is withdrawn.

stories.headline: FCRA Amendment Bill: Comparing India's rules with US and China
stories.summary: A comparative analysis of India's FCRA and the proposed 2026 amendment bill against similar foreign funding regulations in the United States and China, arguing that India's approach reflects global trends in national security oversight rather than being exceptionally restrictive.

stories.headline: Is FCRA 2026 Bill an attack on Christians?
stories.summary: An opinion piece arguing that proposed amendments to the FCRA disproportionately impact Christian NGOs and institutions, particularly in Nagaland where 90% of the population is Christian. The article highlights FCRA cancellation trends, points to perceived double standards in regulation, and questions whether the new Bill unfairly targets religious minorities despite their relatively small share of FCRA registrations.

stories.headline: Assurances not enough, want legal clarity on FCRA Bill: BJP MLA from Meghalaya
stories.summary: A BJP MLA from Meghalaya expresses concerns about an FCRA Bill, stating that government assurances are insufficient and demanding greater legal clarity on the legislation's provisions.

stories.headline: FCRA Bill missing from govt list for Monday | The Shillong Times
stories.summary: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026 was not listed on the government's parliamentary agenda for Monday but debate is expected on August 12. The Bill has triggered widespread controversy, with Christian organisations and state governments from the Northeast, particularly Meghalaya, opposing provisions that would allow government-appointed authorities to manage NGO assets if their FCRA registration is cancelled.

stories.headline: FCRA-Registered NGOs Misused Foreign Funds To Settle Illegal Immigrants, ED Probe Reveals
stories.summary: An ED probe has revealed that FCRA-registered NGOs misused foreign funds to settle illegal immigrants, highlighting enforcement action against regulatory violations by the NGO sector.

stories.headline: Assam Christian Forum Warns FCRA Amendment Could Deal "Death Knell" to NGO Welfare Work
stories.summary: The Assam Christian Forum has expressed concerns that proposed FCRA amendments could severely harm NGO welfare activities in the state, warning of potentially devastating consequences for the non-profit sector's ability to conduct social work.

stories.headline: The FCRA Bill 2026: Balancing National Security and NGO Independence - Ajmal IAS Academy
stories.summary: An opinion piece examining the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, which would allow the government to seize NGO assets and take over management beyond merely cancelling foreign funding licenses, and arguing this shift violates constitutional proportionality doctrine and NGO autonomy rights.

stories.headline: Stricter FCRA Compliance Leaves Only 27.7% of Registered NGOs with Active Licences
stories.summary: Stricter FCRA compliance requirements have resulted in a significant reduction in active NGO licenses, with only 27.7% of registered NGOs retaining active licenses. This highlights the impact of FCRA enforcement on the NGO sector in India.

stories.headline: FCRA registered NGOs down by half in last 10 years; contribution rises from Rs 17832 cr to Rs 22974 cr
stories.summary: The number of FCRA-registered NGOs in India has declined by 50% over the past decade, while foreign contributions to these organizations have increased from Rs 17,832 crore to Rs 22,974 crore. Christian associations received approximately three-quarters of total foreign funding.

stories.headline: FCRA Registration Online in India for NGOs | Ebizfiling
stories.summary: Ebizfiling offers FCRA registration services for NGOs and charitable organisations seeking to receive foreign donations legally in India, with pricing starting at INR 8,999.

stories.headline: Ngo Foreign Donation Restrictions: Fields of work by foreign-funded NGOs outlined, proselytisation excluded | India News - The Times of India
stories.summary: Indian authorities have defined the specific fields of work permitted for foreign-funded NGOs, with restrictions including an explicit exclusion of proselytisation activities. This outlines new or clarified regulatory guidance on FCRA compliance for NGOs receiving international donations.

stories.headline: CBI books US-based missionary group over alleged FCRA violations
stories.summary: The CBI has registered a case against US-based Christian missionary organisation The Timothy Initiative for allegedly spending over Rs 92 crore in foreign funds on missionary activities without FCRA clearances, with operations involving multiple Indian states including Assam, and using fraudulent debit card schemes to circumvent financial regulations.

stories.headline: Explained: What is the FCRA Amendment Bill and why has it sparked a row? | India News - Business Standard
stories.summary: An explanatory article examining the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 currently under parliamentary debate, which proposes major changes including a government-appointed authority to manage foreign contributions and assets when FCRA registrations are cancelled. The amendments have drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties and civil society groups who argue they would give the government sweeping powers over NGOs and institutions.

stories.headline: FCRA bill may impact Christian groups, Nagaland CM tells Amit Shah | India News
stories.summary: The Nagaland Chief Minister has written to the Union Home Minister expressing concerns that proposed FCRA amendments could adversely impact Christian groups and their humanitarian and social service programmes, particularly smaller grassroots organisations in the state. This follows similar concerns raised by CMs from Mizoram and Meghalaya, which are also predominantly Christian states in the Northeast.

stories.headline: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla nominates two RS members to JPC on FCRA Bill as special invitees
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha Speaker has nominated two Rajya Sabha members as special invitees to the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, which proposes stricter oversight of NGOs receiving foreign funds. The committee's first meeting will include a briefing from the Home Ministry on the bill's provisions.

stories.headline: JPC Meeting on FCRA Amendment Bill | Sanjay Jaiswal Leads Panel
stories.summary: A Joint Parliamentary Committee chaired by BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal has begun examining the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, which seeks to tighten regulations on NGO foreign donations and create a designated authority to manage assets of organizations whose FCRA registration expires. Opposition parties and civil society groups, particularly from the North East, have raised concerns about potential impacts on minority-run institutions and NGOs.

stories.headline: FCRA Amendment Bill 2026: Nagaland and Mizoram CMs Demand Joint Parliamentary Committee for FCRA Amendment Bill Review, ETLegalWorld
stories.summary: The Chief Ministers of Nagaland and Mizoram have called for a Joint Parliamentary Committee review of the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, expressing concerns that stricter regulations could adversely impact churches and charitable organizations providing education, healthcare, and social services in their Christian-majority states.

stories.headline: Why Churches in NE opposing FCRA amendment bill?
stories.summary: Church organizations in Northeast India, particularly in Mizoram, are opposing the proposed FCRA amendment bill, with concerns about provisions relating to foreign-funded assets. Church leaders met with the Union Home Minister and submitted memorandums objecting to clauses that could allow government seizure of assets built using foreign funds.

stories.headline: Mizoram govt, churches oppose FCRA Bill, hold statewide prayers
stories.summary: The Mizoram government and churches, particularly the Baptist Church of Mizoram, are actively opposing the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 through statewide prayers and high-level meetings, concerned that the Bill's provisions to seize assets built with foreign funds would threaten church-run schools, hospitals, and welfare centers serving marginalized communities.

stories.headline: India Civic Freedom Monitor - ICNL
stories.summary: ICNL's Civic Freedom Monitor provides a comprehensive overview of India's FCRA regulatory framework, documenting recent restrictive amendments proposed in March 2026 and new rules effective June 2026 that significantly tighten compliance requirements, reporting obligations, and operational restrictions on NGOs receiving foreign contributions.

stories.headline: FCRA 2.0: How India Plans to Rewire Foreign Funding of ...
stories.summary: An article outlining FCRA 2.0 and how India is planning to modify its Foreign Contribution Regulation Act to reshape the framework for foreign funding of NGOs, associations, and individuals.

stories.headline: FCRA NGOs Halve as Foreign Contributions Rise – GKToday
stories.summary: FCRA-registered NGOs have declined sharply from 29,022 in 2015 to 14,466 by September 2026, with over 21,000 cancellations driven primarily by non-compliance with annual reporting requirements, while foreign contributions to these remaining NGOs have actually increased to ₹22,974 crore in 2024-25.

stories.headline: Why Modi government's FCRA Bill is facing pushback
stories.summary: The Modi government's 2026 Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill is facing significant parliamentary opposition over provisions giving a "designated authority" wide control over assets and funds of NGOs whose FCRA registration is cancelled. The bill has been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee after parliamentary deadlock and criticism from opposition parties and state governments.

stories.headline: From charity to development capital: India’s philanthropy moment - The Times of India
stories.summary: An opinion piece examining India's transition from charity-based giving to strategic, institutional philanthropy. The article analyzes the funding gap in India's social sector, discusses the impact of CSR mandates, and proposes solutions including evidence-based impact measurement, diaspora engagement, and stronger partnerships between government, corporations, and NGOs.

stories.headline: India Inc's spending on CSR hits Rs 40,794 cr in FY2024-25: Report - Daily Excelsior
stories.summary: India Inc's CSR spending reached a record Rs 40,794 crore in FY2024-25, marking a 17% year-on-year increase with growing corporate participation and increasing focus on education, healthcare and environmental sustainability across Indian states.

stories.headline: TNM's report on ONGC's donation to RSS-linked organisation: How it misses the 85% to target the 14% in 10 years
stories.summary: This article critiques a report by The News Minutes regarding ONGC's CSR donations to an RSS-linked organisation, arguing that the report's analysis misses broader context about donation distribution patterns over a decade.

stories.headline: Rethinking India's CSR: Bridging the Gap Between Corporate Responsibility and Climate Vulnerability | - The Times of India
stories.summary: A Sattva Consulting report reveals that India's Rs 17,000 crore environmental CSR spending is poorly aligned with climate vulnerability, with vulnerable regions like Jharkhand, Bihar, and West Bengal receiving disproportionately little funding. The article argues that companies must reorient CSR from where implementation is easy to where climate risk is greatest.

stories.headline: PM CARES spent just Rs 88 lakh of its Rs 8,452 crore in 2024-25, put 93% in FD
stories.summary: The PM CARES Fund, despite holding Rs 8,452 crore in assets, spent only Rs 88 lakh (0.001%) in FY 2024-25, with 93% of funds lying idle in fixed deposits while disaster-affected states including Assam seek relief funding. The article highlights transparency concerns around the fund's management and challenges from RTI activists demanding accountability.

stories.headline: Mizoram holds first CSR conclave, CM urges companies to invest in state | Guwahati News - The Times of India
stories.summary: Mizoram's Chief Minister inaugurated the state's first CSR conclave, highlighting the state's favorable conditions for corporate social responsibility projects and urging companies to increase their CSR investments in the state, which currently receives a smaller share of India's estimated Rs 34,000 crore annual CSR funding.

stories.headline: IICA and WNS Global Services launch Ybrant programme to integrate CSR, ESG, and sustainability into management education
stories.summary: IICA and WNS Global Services launched the Ybrant CSR, ESG & Sustainability Programme, a six-month blended learning initiative designed to integrate corporate social responsibility and sustainability principles into management education across five Indian academic institutions.

stories.headline: Assam, Meghalaya CMs seek renewed push for Externally Aided Projects in Northeast India - The Economic Times
stories.summary: The Chief Ministers of Assam and Meghalaya met the Union Finance Minister to seek renewed support for Externally Aided Projects to boost infrastructure development in the Northeast, and received a positive response with assurances of increased investment channels.

stories.headline: Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau
stories.summary: BCPL, a major petrochemical joint venture in Dibrugarh, Assam, has demonstrated significant socio-economic impact through its CSR programmes, which have benefitted over 23,000 people and created 1,692 vocations, while also generating nearly 48,000 livelihoods across its supply chain.

stories.headline: Sistema.bio's EKAFI Biogas Project: Advancing Clean Energy and Sustainable Agriculture in Rural Haryana - TheCSRUniverse
stories.summary: Sistema.bio, in partnership with Escorts Kubota Limited and the EKL CSR Foundation, implemented the EKAFI Biogas Project in Kaithal and Kurukshetra districts of Haryana to provide smallholder farmers with biogas systems that convert livestock waste into clean cooking fuel and organic fertiliser while improving soil health and rural livelihoods.

stories.headline: GTAC hosts charity tea auction for CM’s Relief Fund, unveils Maniram Dewan bust - The Assam Tribune
stories.summary: The Guwahati Tea Auction Centre held a special charity tea auction that raised Rs 2.26 crore for Assam's CM Relief Fund to support flood relief efforts, featuring contributions from major tea companies and ceremonial lots auctioned by the Chief Minister.

stories.headline: Temasek-backed philanthropy group expands India network, backs 2 ventures - Business Standard
stories.summary: Temasek Trust's Philanthropy Asia Alliance is expanding its India network by onboarding Dasra as a new member and backing two impact ventures focused on early childhood education and rural women's economic empowerment. The initiative aims to develop and scale collaborative philanthropy solutions across health, inclusive development, and climate sectors in India and across Asia.

stories.headline: Rajnath Singh urges industry to help PM-SETU develop workforce - The News Mill
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged industry collaboration for PM-SETU, a government-industry-academia partnership to develop a skilled workforce through enhanced ITI training and apprenticeship opportunities aligned with sectors like defence manufacturing, aerospace and electronics.

stories.headline: Nagaland must leverage agriculture, horticulture potential to create jobs: CM Rio - MorungExpress
stories.summary: Nagaland's Chief Minister launched two development initiatives focused on leveraging the state's agriculture, horticulture and creative economy sectors to generate employment and economic growth through enterprise, investment and market linkages.

stories.headline: CSR spending rises as listed firms participation grows
stories.summary: CSR spending by listed Indian companies rose 17.5% to Rs 22,563 crore in FY25, with the number of participating companies growing 20% to 2,013, marking the fastest growth in a decade. The report highlights increased spending on education, healthcare, and notably accelerating investment in environmental and rural development initiatives.

stories.headline: Indian Bank Contributes ₹1.20 Crore for Assam Flood Relief Under CSR, Bank Says I India CSR
stories.summary: Indian Bank has donated ₹1.20 crore towards Assam flood relief efforts as part of its corporate social responsibility obligations, demonstrating corporate sector engagement in disaster response.

stories.headline: Social media critique questions Assam flood relief approach, calls for climate resilience focus
stories.summary: A social media post critiques the use of CSR funds for emergency relief in Assam's recurring floods, arguing that corporate capital should shift from reactive disaster aid to long-term climate resilience and prevention strategies.

stories.headline: How India’s Top FMCG Boards Turn Mandatory CSR Tax into a Strategic Advantage for Risk Management and Brand Trust
stories.summary: An opinion piece analyzing how India's major FMCG companies strategically deploy their mandatory 2% CSR spending to address vulnerabilities in their supply chains and distribution networks, rather than treating it as mere regulatory compliance.

stories.headline: Building on last year's momentum, #Assam continues ...
stories.summary: An Assam-based social media post highlights various Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives and community-focused measures being undertaken in the state, building on momentum from the previous year.

stories.headline: A district level analysis in Assam
stories.summary: Academic analysis examining per capita social sector spending at the district level in Assam, finding it lagged behind the all-state average in 2015-16.

stories.headline: Corporate accountability and formalised corporate social ...
stories.summary: A peer-reviewed academic article examining how India's 2013 Companies Act has shaped CSR implementation by public sector undertakings in the energy sector, finding that while formal accountability mechanisms exist, practices remain compliance-driven with gaps in resource allocation and stakeholder responsiveness.

stories.headline: CSR Spending: Top 10 Companies Invest ₹7,123 Crore; Reliance Industries Ranks First I India CSR
stories.summary: A report on India's top 10 companies' CSR spending patterns, with Reliance Industries leading at ₹7,123 crore in aggregate investment. The article reflects national trends in corporate philanthropy and CSR allocations across India.

stories.headline: The State of CSR in India Report - Sattva Consulting
stories.summary: Sattva Consulting's comprehensive report analyzing seven years of CSR spending trends in India (2014-21), including regional deployment patterns, sectoral allocation, industry-wise investments, and identification of underfunded regions and sectors to guide CSR practitioners and policymakers.

stories.headline: 11th Edition India CSR Outlook Report 2025- CSRBOX
stories.summary: CSRBOX releases its 11th annual India CSR Outlook Report, providing comprehensive analysis of CSR spending trends, priorities, and implementation challenges among 301 leading Indian companies, combining survey data with official disclosures to inform corporate, NGO, and policy stakeholders.

stories.headline: Coal India Limited’s annual CSR spend rises close to Rs 1,000 crore mark | The Shillong Times
stories.summary: Coal India Limited has increased its annual CSR spending to nearly Rs 1,000 crore, exceeding statutory requirements cumulatively by Rs 1,481 crore since 2014-15. The company focuses 90 percent of spending in coal-bearing states and supports multiple sectors including healthcare, education, sanitation, and skill development.

stories.headline: India’s SDGs: The data that’s visible is easy to track but it’s not what ultimately matters | Mint
stories.summary: An opinion piece by India's chief economic advisor and NITI Aayog member arguing that SDG progress should be measured by outcomes and impact on lives rather than by budget size or spending figures. The authors emphasize that businesses, governments, and citizens each have core duties to fulfill effectively—businesses must run ethically before donating to CSR, governments must achieve results efficiently, and citizens must actively participate in development rather than remaining passive recipients.

stories.headline: “Don’t Ask Where the Money Went—Ask What Changed: Meghalaya’s Outcome-Based Budgeting Lesson for India”
stories.summary: Meghalaya's Outcome-Based Budgeting approach uses community feedback mechanisms to shift public health financing from measuring spending to measuring actual results and community-identified health priorities and barriers to service delivery.

stories.headline: CSR Report 2019 - CSRBOX
stories.summary: A comprehensive 2019 research report analyzing CSR spending by 85 companies across North East India in FY 2017-18, showing total CSR spend of INR 342.58 crore (3.6% of India's CSR funds) across 287 projects, with education and skills receiving the largest allocation followed by poverty alleviation and healthcare.

stories.headline: Nagaland explores long term partnership to boost learning in Government schools | India News - The Times of India
stories.summary: Nagaland is pursuing long-term partnerships with Indian and German philanthropic organizations to enhance learning outcomes in government schools, combining domestic and international funding sources for educational improvement.

stories.headline: CAG flags INR 288 cr extra spending in Nagaland’s Jal Jeevan
stories.summary: The CAG's audit of Nagaland identified INR 288 crore in excess spending and multiple financial irregularities in government schemes including Jal Jeevan Mission, MGNREGS, and misuse of development funds for unintended purposes, reflecting broader governance and accountability issues in public fund utilization.

stories.headline: Axis Bank Reports ₹530.11 Crore CSR Obligation Coverage in FY26 - India CSR
stories.summary: Axis Bank reported ₹530.11 crore in CSR obligation coverage for FY26, exceeding its statutory requirement of ₹529.49 crore with a 24.1% increase in spending. The bank's CSR initiatives reached over 21 lakh lives through programmes focused on sustainable livelihoods, financial inclusion, education, healthcare and environmental sustainability.

stories.headline: After rescue, Nagaland’s child protection system faces wider gaps | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com
stories.summary: The article examines systemic gaps in Nagaland's child protection framework, highlighting inadequate funding, staff shortages, infrastructure deficits, and conflicts between customary practices and statutory safeguards that undermine rehabilitation and recovery for rescued children.

stories.headline: ONGC releases corporate social responsibility annual reports
stories.summary: ONGC publishes its CSR annual reports and project lists for multiple financial years. The page is a repository of CSR documentation from a major national public sector undertaking showing its corporate social responsibility spending and initiatives.

stories.headline: Manipur's proactive initiatives to rebuilding lives and communities affected by the conflict - The Economic Times
stories.summary: The Manipur State Government has launched multiple relief and rehabilitation initiatives for communities affected by the ongoing ethnic conflict, including skill training in hospitality, healthcare restoration through partnerships with Apollo Hospital, sports coaching programs, and fragrance formulation training to leverage local medicinal plants for economic development.

stories.headline: /lsapps/loksabhaquestions/annex/188/AU161_1zCBRl.pdf
stories.summary: A Lok Sabha parliamentary question and government response providing five-year CSR expenditure data by state, district, and development sector from FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25, with total CSR spending growing from Rs 26,210.95 crore to Rs 40,794 crore. The response notes that CSR is a board-driven process and the government does not mandate geographic or sector-specific allocations.

stories.headline: Prof. Mahesh Thakur analyzes CSR spending disparities across Indian states from 2022-2024
stories.summary: An analysis of CSR spending trends across Indian states from FY 2022-2024 highlights stark regional disparities, with states like Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura experiencing sharp declines while Gujarat and Kerala see major growth, raising concerns about equitable distribution of CSR funding to regions with greatest need.

stories.headline: Northeast India Nonprofits: The Basecamp Initiative 2026 Support | Samyak posted on the topic | LinkedIn
stories.summary: Samyak Partners is launching The Basecamp Initiative 2026, a month-long capacity-building program offering no-cost support to emerging NGOs across the eight North East states to strengthen their fundraising readiness and institutional systems. Applications close on August 10th for eligible organizations with ₹1.5–10 crore annual budgets and three years of operational history.

stories.headline: Kruse calls for shift from subsistence to sustainable agriculture in Nagaland - MorungExpress
stories.summary: Nagaland's Minister for Women Resource Development and Horticulture calls for sustainable agriculture and greater support for farmers through government schemes, training, and market linkages. The fair organized by a local community group showcases organic farming and entrepreneurship initiatives that have evolved into a successful model for economic self-reliance.

stories.headline: Expanding definitions of generosity: Global and U.S. trends in helping others
stories.summary: GivingTuesday's State of Generosity report reveals global and U.S. giving trends, highlighting that India and Kenya lead in civic commitment to helping others, and that remittances ($690 billion) far exceed government and philanthropic aid. The analysis shows resilience in generosity across multiple forms, with U.S. data showing increases in donations, volunteering, and a growing willingness to support those with different viewpoints.

stories.headline: What if CSR stopped working in silos?
stories.summary: The article examines why CSR funding tends to concentrate in certain geographies across India and proposes that better coordination among funders could lead to more equitable distribution and outcomes.

stories.headline: UNICEF: Children ‘invisible’ in Asia’s corporate philanthropy reporting  - Alliance magazine
stories.summary: A UNICEF study finds that corporate sustainability reporting across Asia, including India, fails to adequately identify or measure impacts on children, despite children making up a third of the region's population and companies reporting child-related philanthropic activities.

stories.headline: From savings to self-reliance: How SHGs are transforming rural Uttar Pradesh - The Times of India
stories.summary: The article chronicles how Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in Uttar Pradesh have evolved into a major force for rural women's financial inclusion and entrepreneurship, with over 1.05 crore women mobilized into nearly 9 lakh SHGs and thousands trained as banking correspondents to bring financial services to villages.

stories.headline: Why philanthropy may not be the fix everyone wants it to be | The Social Enterprise Magazine - Pioneers Post
stories.summary: An OECD policy analyst discusses why private philanthropy is not replacing declining official development assistance and highlights data gaps in Asian giving, particularly regarding climate funding and coordination between international and domestic foundations.

stories.headline: Union govt has no central data on unspent CSR funds, no policy for equitable distribution: Govt tells Parliament
stories.summary: The Union government admitted in Parliament that it does not maintain centralised data on unspent CSR funds and has no policy to ensure equitable distribution of CSR spending across states, leaving such decisions entirely to company boards. The admission drew criticism for lack of transparency and accountability in CSR implementation.

stories.headline: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 Introduced: Push For Decriminalisation And Easier Compliance - BW Legal World
stories.summary: The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026 proposes significant changes to CSR regulations, including increasing the net profit threshold for CSR applicability from Rs 5 crore to Rs 10 crore, extending the timeline for unspent CSR fund transfers from 30 to 90 days, and raising maximum non-compliance penalties to Rs 1 crore, while also providing relief for small companies and startups.

stories.headline: Ratlam professor cheating case leads MP police to international syndicate, fake NGOs
stories.summary: An international cyber crime racket operating from Cambodia used fake NGOs and shell companies to launder Rs 1.34 crore extorted from a retired Madhya Pradesh professor. The multi-state investigation revealed fake NGOs were opened only on paper to serve as mule accounts, with networks also extending to Assam.

stories.headline: Illiterate youth from rural Assam trafficked on pretext of jobs: SSB | Guwahati News - The Times of India
stories.summary: SSB and an NGO partner, Assam Centre for Rural Development (ACRD), helped rescue 115 trafficking victims from rural Assam who had been lured with false job promises to Bihar. The case highlights an organized trafficking network targeting underprivileged youth, with nine traffickers arrested so far.

stories.headline: Assam Police Arrest Two in Kerala Over Rs 50-Lakh Scam
stories.summary: Dibrugarh Police arrested two individuals in Kerala in connection with a Rs 50-lakh financial fraud scam that originated in Assam, with investigations suggesting a multi-state criminal network.

stories.headline: 37 global groups urge Assam govt to free Doley, drop charges against 4 others
stories.summary: Thirty-seven international civil society and human rights organisations have called for the release of indigenous rights activist Pranab Doley, detained under the National Security Act in Assam, and the withdrawal of charges against four others arrested during protests against a proposed hotel project at Kaziranga that allegedly violates Adivasi land rights and environmental protections.

stories.headline: Fake QR Codes, Donation Scams: Assam’s Flood Relief Faces a Trust Crisis
stories.summary: Flood relief efforts in Assam are being undermined by donation scams involving fake QR codes, raising serious concerns about trust in NGOs and charitable organizations handling disaster relief funds.

stories.headline: ED chargesheets self-styled godman Ashok Kharat in money laundering case - The New Indian Express
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has filed a chargesheet against self-styled godman Ashok Kharat and associates for money laundering, alleging he exploited religious devotees through fraudulent schemes and coercive tactics. The investigation revealed Rs 37 crore in seized assets and fraudulent transactions routed through cooperative societies and benami accounts across multiple states.

stories.headline: ‘No place to breathe’: AISA’s Neha Bora detained again, alleges police brutality - The Times of India
stories.summary: AISA president Neha Bora was detained during anti-CEC protests in Delhi and alleged police brutality, including cramped detention conditions and violence against male protesters.

stories.headline: AJYCP seeks extension of Assam Census 2027 self-enumeration deadline after floods - The Assam Tribune
stories.summary: An NGO (AJYCP) has petitioned the Centre to extend the Census 2027 self-enumeration deadline for Assam and demanded expedited housing and livelihood support for families affected by recent floods that have disrupted utilities and document access.

stories.headline: Why an indigenous community in Arunachal blacklisted four researchers
stories.summary: An indigenous community organization in Arunachal Pradesh's Dibang Valley blacklisted four researchers for violating its code of research ethics, including conducting fieldwork without final approval. The incident highlights tensions around research governance and community consent in protected cultural areas.

stories.headline: Scientology relief team distributes aid in flood-hit Assam
stories.summary: An international relief team from Scientology is conducting humanitarian operations in flood-affected areas of Assam, distributing water, food, and medicines to affected communities.

stories.headline: India’s NGOs at a new funding crossroads
stories.summary: An opinion piece examining the changing funding landscape for India's NGOs and the critical juncture they face in securing financial support.

stories.headline: 6th KSU functionary held over Aug 19 Shillong violence - The Times of India
stories.summary: The sixth member of the Khasi Students' Union (KSU) has been arrested in connection with violence and vandalism during a student protest bike rally in Shillong on August 19, with previous arrests including top KSU leadership. The incident resulted in two vehicles set on fire, 31 vandalized, and 18 people assaulted.

stories.headline: Arambai Tenggol, village volunteers not banned organisations: Manipur CM
stories.summary: Manipur's Chief Minister clarified that village volunteer groups and the Meitei organization Arambai Tenggol are not banned, and arrests are made based on criminal activities rather than group affiliation. The government is examining cases related to violence that began in May 2023 and reaffirmed its 2024 policy not to prosecute youths uninvolved in serious crimes.

stories.headline: Three arrested for extortion, cadre recruitment for banned outfits in Manipur - The Hindu
stories.summary: Three members of banned militant outfits—the People's Liberation Army and PREPAK—have been arrested in Manipur for extortion and illegal cadre recruitment activities.

stories.headline: A multi-departmental awareness programme on child ...
stories.summary: Four facilitators have been arrested in connection with what appears to be a child protection programme, with investigation suggesting further criminal links.

stories.headline: Tighter regime proposed: FCRA Bill seeks custodian for NGO assets
stories.summary: A proposed FCRA bill introduces stricter requirements for NGOs receiving foreign funding, including mandatory custodian oversight of assets and tighter restrictions on their use and geographical scope, with assets potentially vesting to a government authority if registration lapses.

stories.headline: NGOs rally behind KSU, slam govt’s ‘indifferent attitude’ to five-point demand
stories.summary: Multiple civil society organisations in Meghalaya, including FKJGP, HNYF and JSU, have rallied behind the Khasi Students' Union to criticise the state government's inaction on their five-point demands and condemned police action against KSU leaders, citing government indifference and alleged misuse of authority.

stories.headline: Police stations not for press meets by political parties, NGOs: High Court | Highland Post
stories.summary: A High Court ruling restricts the use of police stations for press meets by political parties and NGOs, indicating judicial oversight of NGO activities and public space usage in Meghalaya.

stories.headline: Meghalaya Congress holds protest in Shillong against proposed FCRA amendments
stories.summary: The Meghalaya Pradesh Congress Committee organized a protest in Shillong against proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), expressing concerns that the new provisions could adversely impact churches, educational institutions, and NGOs receiving foreign funding, particularly through property attachment clauses.

stories.headline: Why 20,701 NGOs lost their FCRA licences since 1976: Cause, impact decoded | Personal Finance - Business Standard
stories.summary: The article explains the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 and examines why over 20,700 NGOs have lost their FCRA licences since 1976, with recent focus on the cancellation of prominent organizations' licences over allegations of misusing foreign donations.

stories.headline: CAG flags fund misuse, unfinished works across Nagaland
stories.summary: A CAG audit report on Nagaland government departments for 2022-23 reveals widespread financial irregularities, including misused funds, stalled projects and weak oversight across healthcare, worker welfare, policing and other sectors. The findings highlight systemic governance failures and call for recovery of misused funds and strengthened financial controls.

stories.headline: FCRA bill debate likely on Aug 12: Mizoram CM | India News
stories.summary: The Mizoram Chief Minister reports that a parliamentary debate on the FCRA bill is expected to take place on August 12, indicating ongoing legislative action on foreign funding regulations affecting NGOs.

stories.headline: Mizoram churches protest FCRA Bill, warn of property seizure if passed in current form - The Economic Times
stories.summary: Churches in Mizoram held a protest rally against the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, warning that the amendments could lead to asset and property seizure for churches and NGOs if passed in its current form.

stories.headline: CAG suspects Rs 9.19-crore GIM fund misappropriation in Mizoram’s Kolasib
stories.summary: The CAG has flagged suspected misappropriation of Rs 9.19 crore released under the Green India Mission in Mizoram's Kolasib district, with no documentary evidence that the funds reached intended village-level committees and recommendations for a government investigation.

stories.headline: Women's power driving self-reliant Tripura: 221 SHGs hold AGM in Kalyanpur Block - Tripuratimes
stories.summary: An Annual General Meeting of 221 self-help groups in Kalyanpur Block, Tripura, convened to review progress on women's economic empowerment and livelihoods, and to plan future strategies for expanding entrepreneurship and income-generation opportunities in rural communities.

stories.headline: Assam minister reviews post-flood agriculture rehabilitation in Charaideo - The News Mill
stories.summary: An Assam minister visited Charaideo district to review post-flood agricultural rehabilitation efforts, including paddy seed distribution programs coordinated with the NGO AAMI to help affected farmers resume cultivation.

stories.headline: Two MHA officials arrested for seeking ‘illegal gratification’ for FCRA registration - The Hindu
stories.summary: Two Ministry of Home Affairs officials have been arrested for allegedly demanding bribes to facilitate FCRA (Foreign Contribution Regulation Act) registration for NGOs. This reveals corruption within the regulatory system that directly impacts NGOs' ability to obtain FCRA clearance.

stories.headline: Details of NGO Empanelment
stories.summary: AJAGAR SOCIAL CIRCLE has been empaneled by NERCORMS (North Eastern Region Community Resource Management Society) for the period 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2029, with empanelment number NERCORMS/EMP/NGO/2026/01.

stories.headline:
🌿Welcome Society for North East Handmade Paper Development🌿
We are delighted to welcome Society for @North East Handmade Paper Development for Varsha Mangal Mahotsav 2026 and the National Mission… | Shaweta Berry
stories.summary: Society for North East Handmade Paper Development is welcomed as a partner in Varsha Mangal Mahotsav 2026, a national tree-planting mission to plant 45 lakh trees in 45 days (22 July–4 September 2026) with the goal of setting an India Book of Records.

stories.headline: Empowering livelihoods through sustainable innovation. 🌿 ...
stories.summary: A social media post highlights how a Handmade Paper Unit at Melli, supported by the North Eastern Council, is creating employment opportunities and strengthening local communities through sustainable livelihoods.

stories.headline: KABIL conducts fisheries training in Udalguri to boost sustainable livelihoods
stories.summary: KABIL conducted two fisheries training programmes in Udalguri district to strengthen sustainable livelihoods and rural development, partnering with the Department of Fisheries and Krishi Vigyan Kendra to train villagers in modern fish farming practices.

stories.headline: KABIL board members visit Assam blocks to assess sustainable livelihood projects
stories.summary: KABIL's Board Members conducted field visits to Majbat and Udalguri blocks in Assam on 12-13 September 2026 to observe the progress of livelihood, agriculture, livestock and natural resource management interventions, including vermicompost beds, solar panels, integrated farming systems, and community-led development projects.

stories.headline: KABIL hosts joint field visit to showcase sustainable rural livelihoods project in Udalguri
stories.summary: KABIL hosted a joint field visit by Azim Premji Foundation and Bharat Rural Livelihoods Foundation leadership to DWIMU project sites in Christianpara Village, Udalguri Block, showcasing community engagement and grassroots interventions in sustainable rural livelihoods including fishery, poultry, piggery, and arecanut plantation units.

stories.headline: KABIL coordinates village development planning across 20 VCDCs in Udalguri district
stories.summary: KABIL participated in Gaon Sabha meetings across 20 VCDCs in Udalguri district on Gandhi Jayanti to coordinate participatory village development planning, including priority plan submission and village governance programme formulation with community engagement.

stories.headline: Axis Bank partners with SSAIT to set up India’s first fully integrated Olympic-standard Archery Centre in rural India
stories.summary: Axis Bank Foundation has partnered with Sanjeeva Singh Archery Institute Trust to develop India's first fully integrated Olympic-standard archery centre in rural Uttar Pradesh, providing world-class training infrastructure and residential facilities to talented athletes from underserved regions over a three-year period.

stories.headline: DAY-NRLM Launches National Compendium on Rural Livelihoods
stories.summary: The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission, with support from Axis Bank Foundation, launched a National Compendium documenting convergence approaches and field experiences in rural livelihoods across 19 Indian states, showcasing sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural women.

stories.headline: Azim Premji Foundation’s Janato Cinema Backs Socially Conscious Indian Films and Emerging Directors
stories.summary: The Azim Premji Foundation has launched Janato Cinema, a new initiative backing socially conscious films and emerging filmmakers, with an inaugural slate of short films that premiered at the Bengaluru International Short Film Festival, including works by Oscar-nominated director Shaunak Sen.

stories.headline: Azim Premji Scholarship 2026: Registration begins at azimpremjifoundation.org, check who can apply | Education
stories.summary: Azim Premji Foundation has opened registration for the Azim Premji Scholarship 2026, with details available on their official website. The news article provides eligibility information and registration details for interested applicants.

stories.headline: Azim Premji Foundation Report June 2026
stories.summary: The Azim Premji Foundation report for June 2026 announces scholarship renewals for cohorts 2024 and 2025, and invites applications for a resource person position, indicating ongoing funding and recruitment activities by the foundation.

stories.headline: SBI Foundation announces ₹100 crore scholarship for over 25,000 students - The Hindu
stories.summary: SBI Foundation announces the launch of its Platinum Jubilee Asha Scholarship 2026, a major corporate scholarship programme providing annual grants of ₹15,000 to ₹15,00,000 to over 25,000 meritorious students from disadvantaged backgrounds across India studying at various academic levels. Applications opened on July 22, 2026.

stories.headline: IIT Madras, SBI Foundation launch phase 2 of Para-Athlete Sports Scholarship Programme | Indian Institute of Technology Madras
stories.summary: SBI Foundation in partnership with IIT Madras has launched Phase 2 of its Para-Athlete Sports Scholarship Programme, expanding support to 80 para-athletes across eight Paralympic disciplines with monthly stipends of ₹40,000 and sports science-based performance assessments, building on Phase 1's success where scholars won 70 medals in national and international competitions.

stories.headline: IIT Bombay Hubs and CoEs - SBI Foundation Hub for Data Science and Analytics - Indian Institute of Technology Bombay
stories.summary: The SBI Foundation has established a hub for data science and analytics at IIT Bombay's Centre for Machine Intelligence and Data Science, supporting research in generative AI, safe AI systems, and digital interfaces with applications to banking challenges.

stories.headline: SBI Foundation and CBM India Project Restores Sight to Thousands- CSRBOX
stories.summary: SBI Foundation partnered with CBM India Project to restore sight to thousands of people, demonstrating the foundation's healthcare impact work.

stories.headline: Tata Trusts is moving towards building institutions, from just funding projects, says its Chairman, Noel Tata - The Hindu
stories.summary: Noel Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, announces a strategic shift from project-based funding to building permanent institutions in healthcare and education, including plans for 40-50 not-for-profit general hospitals and world-class higher education institutions across India.

stories.headline: Tata Trusts Seeks New Way Around Tata Sons Listing - Bloomberg
stories.summary: Tata Trusts, as majority shareholder of Tata Sons, submitted a reorganization proposal to merge two subsidiary companies into Tata Sons to convert it from a holding company into an operating entity. This reflects governance and structural developments within the Tata group.

stories.headline: An intense boardroom battle is brewing at India's giant Tata Group
stories.summary: Tata Trusts, led by Noel Tata, is embroiled in a boardroom dispute with Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran over his reappointment and diverging strategic visions regarding company listing and capital allocation. The conflict reflects fundamental disagreements about business growth strategy, ownership preservation, and regulatory compliance.

stories.headline: Why Tata Trusts Should Let Go Of Tata Sons - Rediff.com Business
stories.summary: An opinion piece arguing that Tata Trusts should divest its controlling stake in Tata Sons to resolve structural tensions between philanthropic and commercial interests, allowing Tata Trusts to build a larger corpus for charitable activities while freeing the commercial arm from conflicting priorities.

stories.headline: Noel Tata Tells Arnab How Tata Trusts Separates Philanthropy From Controlling Stake | Business News
stories.summary: Noel Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, discusses in an interview how the trusts maintain a clear separation between their philanthropic mandate and their role as controlling shareholder of Tata Sons. He explains that Tata Sons serves as the financial engine generating dividends to grow the trust corpus at 20% annually, which funds philanthropic activities in healthcare, education, and skill development.

stories.headline: Embattled Tata Patriarch Faces Revolt at Charities He Helms - Bloomberg
stories.summary: A governance dispute has emerged within Tata Trusts, with two vice-chairmen of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust challenging patriarch Noel Tata over a restructuring plan they claim was advanced without proper consultation or trustee meetings.

stories.headline: Rural Development Projects - CSRBOX
stories.summary: Tata Trusts' Transforming Rural India (TRI) initiative works toward large-scale rural transformation in villages across Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh, targeting regions of endemic poverty.

stories.headline: [PDF] Lifting Rural Farmers Out of Poverty: Lakhpati Kisan - Bridgespan
stories.summary: A Bridgespan profile of the Lakhpati Kisan initiative, documenting Tata Trusts' flagship rural livelihoods programme in Central India that aims to lift tribal farming households out of poverty through community-led income enhancement interventions, with INR 120 crores in funding over five years.

stories.headline: Tata Trusts CEO Highlights Nation-Building Legacy, Healthcare Access and Community Resilience I India CSR
stories.summary: An India CSR article highlights Tata Trusts' CEO discussing the organisation's nation-building legacy, healthcare access initiatives, and community resilience work.

stories.headline: Bodoland Development Foundation mourns death of missing 20-year-old woman
stories.summary: A social media post from Bodoland Development Foundation announces the tragic death of a 20-year-old Boro woman from Bonda, Guwahati who went missing.

stories.headline: Bodoland Development Foundation | Organisation Profile | The CSR Universe
stories.summary: This is a directory listing page for Bodoland Development Foundation on The CSR Universe website, a platform tracking CSR and social impact organisations in India. The page is primarily navigation and subscription prompts with limited substantive information about BDF itself.

stories.headline: Apply to Finance - Bhopal Job at Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh ...
stories.summary: Azim Premji Foundation is recruiting for a Finance position in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. The foundation works to improve school education quality in India through teacher support.

stories.headline: Faculty position in Social Sciences (Political Economy, Labour, and Livelihoods)
stories.summary: Azim Premji University is recruiting a full-time faculty member in Social Sciences with focus on Political Economy, Labour and Livelihoods at its Bengaluru campus, seeking candidates with advanced training in quantitative research methods.

stories.headline: Peacebuilding through Community Development in Rural India
stories.summary: A LinkedIn post by RamG Vallath, Chief Editor of The Health Worker podcast by Azim Premji Foundation, profiles the Tribal Health Initiative in Tamil Nadu's Sittilingi Valley, highlighting its achievements in reducing infant and maternal mortality through integrated healthcare and community development. The post mentions Azim Premji Foundation as the producer of the podcast featuring this organization's work.

stories.headline: Drama Without a Stage: Theatre Education Techniques for ...
stories.summary: An educational article on theatre techniques in classrooms cites Azim Premji Foundation's open-access research as a free resource for teachers, alongside other government initiatives and support services. The foundation is mentioned as providing research-based materials to support experiential learning in Indian schools.

stories.headline: Azim Premji donates 50,000 crore to charity
stories.summary: Azim Premji announced a major donation of 50,000 crore to charity, demonstrating significant philanthropic commitment through his foundation.

stories.headline: Putul Sonowal makes history by confirming India's first-ever ...
stories.summary: SBI Foundation partners with Special Olympics Bharat to operate 15 training centres across India, providing support to over 750 athletes with intellectual disabilities.

stories.headline: Day 1 Today's topic: Why poultry farming is an attractive ...
stories.summary: KABIL facilitated distribution of 5,000 chicks to 51 women farmers in Udalguri and Mazbat blocks as part of the 4th phase of a poultry farming initiative.

stories.headline: KABIL announces job recruitment drive in Udalguri, Assam
stories.summary: KABIL, the NGO based in Udalguri, Assam, announced a job recruitment campaign on LinkedIn with hashtags referencing the organisation, Udalguri, and Mazbat, directing applicants to submit via a Google Form.

The light material of silk was sometimes used as a recording medium, but was normally too expensive to consider. The Han dynasty Chinese court official Cai Lun (c. 50–121 CE) is credited as the inventor of a method of papermaking (inspired by wasps and bees) using rags and other plant fibers in 105 CE. However, the discovery of specimens bearing written Chinese characters in 2006 at Fangmatan in north-east China's Gansu Province suggests that paper was in use by the ancient Chinese military more than 100 years before Cai, [...] in the Italian Province of Ferrara introduced Fabriano artisans in the Province of Ancona[clarification needed] the technique of making paper by hand. links.snippet:
Where and when to see flying ants?

The answer is virtually anywhere during July and August. Black ants are very adaptable and can be found in a huge range of urban and rural locations – if you have a garden you are likely to have black ants. Often the first thing to spot will be the activity of gulls or swifts circling as they begin to pick off the ants as they rise into the air. The whole spectacle can last an hour or more. Hot summer days with little wind and no rain seem to act as a trigger to ants taking to the wing.

## What is FCRA?

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 regulates the acceptance and utilisation of foreign contributions in India. It applies to NGOs, trusts, societies, educational institutions, religious organisations and certain other entities that receive funding from foreign sources.

Under the law, any organisation seeking to receive foreign contributions must obtain registration, or prior permission, from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

Police sources said that multiple cases had already been registered against him earlier. In 2024, he was arrested by Silchar police in connection with similar fraud cases in the Barak Valley.

Gogoi is also accused of running fake companies and cheating people in the name of finance and business schemes. Even after coming out of jail, he allegedly continued similar activities, including fraud in the name of loans and vehicle rentals.

Fresh cases have also been registered against him in Rangia, Sonapur and Garchuk police stations.

Nagaland, one of India's smaller states, is located in the hills and mountains of the northeastern part of the country. It is bordered by Arunachal Pradesh to the northeast, Manipur to the south, Assam to the west and northwest, and Myanmar to the east. links.snippet:
In 2024, industrialist S. P. Oswal was reportedly defrauded of ₹7 crore after criminals created an elaborate virtual proceeding. The fraudsters allegedly displayed a fake arrest warrant, forged official papers, and a fabricated Supreme Court order. They even arranged a virtual courtroom to make the proceedings appear genuine. Police subsequently arrested suspects and recovered a substantial part of the transferred money.

• Scientific Method (in kid form): Question → Hypothesize → Test → Observe → Refine. This builds critical thinking, resilience to failure, and genuine understanding rather than memorization. A child wondering “Why do leaves change color?” can observe trees over weeks, compare samples, or do simple experiments with leaves and light. It turns curiosity into structured discovery.
• Observation: Direct sensory experience creates richer mental models than secondhand explanations. Watching ants, mixing colors, or tracking the moon’s phases sticks better because it engages multiple senses and emotions. [...] • Leadership – Taking initiative, guiding a team, and learning that being in charge is often harder than doing the task yourself.

Indian teachers already sense that the research on classroom drama techniques is more specific and more useful than most professional development programmes suggest; it just rarely gets said aloud in a staffroom. Originally, the ancient region was a federation composed of three distinct Phoenician coastal cities: Oea (modern-day Tripoli), Leptis Magna, and Sabratha.   
  
When the Vandals invaded the region and destroyed the defensive walls of Sabratha and Leptis Magna, those cities eventually crumbled into ruins. Oea, however, managed to withstand the invasions, grew in importance, and inherited the collective name of all three.

SELCO Foundation on Instagram: "What does it take to make climate-smart livelihood solutions more accessible to rural entrepreneurs?

On October 6, 2026, SELCO Foundation and DIYA Foundation, in collaboration with Assam Gramin Bank (AGB), organised a Bankers’ Orientation Workshop on Financing Climate-Smart & DRE-Enabled Livelihood Solutions in Kamrup, bringing together banking officials, clean-energy technology providers and rural entrepreneurs.

The workshop explored how bank finance can support smallholder farmers, women-led enterprises and micro-entrepreneurs in adopting productive-use technologies. Through technology showcases, field experiences and discussions on loan structuring, participants examined ways to address financing barriers, manage lending risks and align bank credit with government schemes and subsidies.

This marks the first structured engagement under the MoU between AGB and the two organisations, laying the groundwork for stronger financing pathways for climate-smart livelihoods across Kamrup and beyond.
